title: Godot's UI scale changes across monitors on Wayland multi-monitor multi-resolution setup
body: ### Tested versions Current Godot version: 4.7.2 But this bug was there for as long as I can remember ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - cpe:/o:nixos:nixos:26.11 #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Jul 4 11:44:22 UTC 2026 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 4 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (nvidia; 595.84) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13400F (16 threads) - 31.18 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When I run Godot with Wayland enabled, the Godot UI changes size when moving from one screen to another. My monitors have different resolutions: 1920x1080 and 3840x2160, and the 3840x2160 monitor has scailing 200%, so it is treated as 1920x1080 monitor. So Godot must have the same size on all monitors (just like all other Wayland applications) Video with sound https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5067b8bc-997b-486c-8db5-fc798f8501a5 ### Steps to reproduce If you don't have Linux PC, you can use Live USB for test 1. Go to [nixos.org/download](https://nixos.org/download/) and download Graphical ISO image 2. Write an ISO Image to a USB Disk 3. Boot using KDE Plasma (for example) On Linux PC or Live USB 1. Connect 2 different monitors (for example 1920x1080 and 3840x2160) 2. RMB on Desktop > Display Configuration > Set 3840x2160 monitor's scaling to 2, so that both monitors would have the same scale, but different resolution 3. Install Godot using Konsole ```bash nix-shell -p godot godot ``` 4. In Godot enable `Editor Settings > Run > Platforms > Prefer Wayland` 5. Move windows between monitors If nothing is happening, relaunch Godot one more time, to make sure Wayland version is launched. You can check if Godot uses Wayland using KWin Debug Console ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
